question: Explain why the plates of a charged parallel plate capacitor may be treated as equipotential surfaces and why the electric field between them is normal to the plates. If the plate separation is doubled while the capacitor remains connected to the same battery, determine the change in electric field, capacitance, charge and energy stored.

options.A: The plates are not equipotential because electric field exists inside them. On doubling separation with battery connected, $E$, $C$, $Q$, and $U$ all double.
options.B: The plates are equipotential, but electric field is parallel to them. On doubling separation, $E$ remains same, $C$ doubles, $Q$ doubles and $U$ doubles.
options.C: Each conducting plate is an equipotential surface because $E=0$ inside a conductor. Electric field lines are normal to equipotential surfaces, so the field between plates is normal to the plates. With the same battery connected, $V$ remains constant; doubling $d$ makes $E=V/d$, $C=\varepsilon_0A/d$, $Q=CV$, and $U=\dfrac12CV^2$ each become half.
options.D: On doubling separation with the battery connected, $E$ and $C$ become half but $Q$ and $U$ remain unchanged.
